items.title: Whether a reading's location and protocol belong on the assertion, when corroboration is counted by assertions
items.why: KWB-47 declared a contract carrying where in a source something was read and under what protocol, and KWB-53 established that admission discards both -- so the invariant that every admitted claim identifies its source occurrence and extraction protocol is unmet, and there is no record of the decision that would settle how. The obvious move is to put them on the Assertion, and it is the wrong one in a way that is only visible once corroboration is counted: this repository counts corroboration by assertions. The test that exercises the mechanism every identity decision here was made to support says so -- two different documents, the same claim text, one claim and two assertions, each naming the address of the document it was read out of. If lineage entered an assertion's identity, re-reading one book under a new prompt would produce a second assertion for the same claim from the same source, and the count that says two sources agree would say two when one source was read twice. That is the reference miner's measured failure reached from the other direction: its claim identity absorbs the source path and page window, so two sources' assertions can never meet. And carrying them without identifying by them is the other failure, KWB-32's: two readings meeting at one assertion that holds one of their lineages is a value disagreeing with itself.
items.done_when: A record decides where a reading's location and protocol live and what may never absorb them, with the corroboration-count argument as its measurement rather than as a preference. It states the consequence of each rejected placement in terms of something this repository already measured. If the answer is that provenance about a reading is its own thing rather than a field on an existing one, the record says what that costs, what it does not decide, and the condition that settles the rest -- the shape D-012 and D-014 use, where a decision names the consumer whose absence defers the build. It does not build it: nothing here reads a source yet, every reading is a person through Stated, and a mechanism built before its consumer is what D-009 and the queue in D19 are both about. Relations are declared so the contract test finds them from both ends.

items.title: Eleven canonical records say their back-link section is generated and that the test fails if it is wrong, and neither half is true
items.why: Every record that is the target of a declared relation carries a note reading 'Generated by tests/contract, which fails if it is wrong.' Nothing generates it. The test reads the target and asks whether its text contains the source identifier anywhere; it writes nothing. I hand-appended three of these sections in the previous iteration, which is the proof. The second half is false in a way that matters more: the check passes on any mention anywhere in the target, so a Referenced By list can be stale, incomplete or list records that do not relate at all and the test stays green -- it fails when a target never names a source, not when the section is wrong. Eleven copies of one false premise in canonical records is the shape of the defect this repository has chased three times, and this one is worse than the retired compile premise because the note is self-authenticating: it explains the KWB-38 measurement, so a reader has every reason to trust it and conclude the section maintains itself. A session authoring a record would then not add the back-link, and would read a stale section as current.
items.done_when: The note says what actually happens: the section is written by hand and checked by tests/contract. The check earns the second half rather than the wording being softened to match a weak test -- a declared relation must be answered by an entry in the target's Referenced By section rather than by any mention anywhere in its text, and an entry in a section that no record declares a relation to is caught too, so the claim that it fails if it is wrong is true in both directions. Measured to discriminate in both directions before the wording is trusted. All eleven relation targets already carry the section, so nothing is restructured to make the stricter check pass; if that turns out to be false for any record, the record is fixed rather than the check loosened. The malformed section added in the previous iteration is corrected: its list is separated from the paragraph above it and its dashes match the other ten.

items.title: The first sentence of the document that answers what exists states three capabilities in the present tense, and the repository has one of them
items.why: AGENTS.md routes 'What exists, what owns what' to README.md, and tests/contract asserts its bands table in both directions. Its prose is asserted by nothing, and its opening sentence says KWB ingests references and builds a durable graph of the concepts they teach, the claims they assert, and the code that implements them. The graph is real: admission, publication and replay build it and it survives a process. The other two are not. Nothing in this repository reads a source -- KWB-47 declared the extraction contract and its only implementation is Stated, a person typing through --says, so what the graph holds is what a person said a reference asserts and not what the reference teaches. KWB-47's own why named this sentence as the thing that cannot be true and could not fix it, because its territory was kwb-ingest and kwb-cli. And there is no code entity at all: the domain is Concept, Claim and Assertion, Publication carries those three, no type mentions code or implementation, and D-004 does not hold the subject either -- so it is a capability with no entity, no decision and no item, stated in the present tense in the document a session is told to trust for what exists. A canonical document asserting what the repository does not do is the stale-premise defect one level above the code, which is what the record-reachability guard exists for and what the bands table is checked for; the prose between them was never looked at.
items.done_when: The opening says what this repository does today and what it intends, and a reader can tell which is which without leaving the paragraph. Ingestion is stated as what it is -- a source is admitted and what it asserts is supplied by a reader, and the only reader is a person -- with the contract that will change that named. The code capability is stated as intent and not as behaviour, and says plainly that nothing here represents code and no record has decided it, rather than being deleted so that a reader cannot tell it was ever meant. The graph claim is left alone: it is true. No new decision is taken here, because deciding whether KWB represents code is a record and not a README edit, and this item reserves README.md alone.

items.title: The eaten-continuation scanner reads Rust only, and the fifth instance landed in the one command a reader is told to type
items.why: KWB-52 built a scanner for a literal whose line continuation was eaten by a scripted edit, and it reads .rs files under crates/. KWB-56 found the fifth instance outside that reach: both kwb admit lines in README.md's Trying it section carried seven spaces before --says, in the only command a new reader is asked to run. The scanner would never have seen it. The damage is a property of an edit, not of a language -- anything a scripted edit writes can lose a continuation, and a console block is the worst place for it to land because a reader copies it. Markdown is not Rust, so the Rust rule does not transfer: indentation is meaningful in markdown, tables are aligned deliberately, and a fenced block holds text whose layout is its content. A scan that flagged those would be turned off, which is the failure mode KWB-52's own exemptions were written against.
items.done_when: A guard fails on a run of spaces in the middle of a command line inside a fenced console block anywhere under docs/ and in README.md and AGENTS.md. It reads only the command lines of console fences, because that is where the damage lands and where a reader copies from, and it says why it does not scan markdown generally -- deliberate alignment, meaningful indentation, and fenced content whose layout is the point. Each exemption is demonstrated by a real shape from these files rather than described. It is shown to detect the instance KWB-56 fixed, reconstructed, and the reader is asserted to have found the files and the fences, because a scanner that reads nothing passes everywhere. If it flags anything else in the tree, that is a finding and is fixed rather than exempted.

items.title: The Rust scanner's threshold is justified by a sample of damage rather than by the structure, which is the reasoning that produced a wrong threshold one item later
items.why: KWB-52's literal scanner sets its threshold at eight and justifies it by the magnitudes of the damage it had seen: the five real instances carried ten, ten, ten, ten and eighteen. KWB-57 then carried that same number to markdown command lines and it was wrong -- the real instance there carried seven, the guard reported clean on it, and its own detector test passed because the fixture was a reconstruction carrying ten. The number here is not wrong, but its stated reason is the same reasoning, and it is stale besides: there are six known instances now and one of them carried seven. Reasoning from a sample of damage says nothing about what the guard will meet next, because the magnitude of this damage is the source indentation of whatever line it happened to, which is a property of the code and not of the defect. Measured properly, tree-wide: the largest run of spaces inside a literal of thirty or more characters is five, in a printed table column, and every continuation site in crates has an indent of nine, thirteen or seventeen. Those two numbers are what bound a safe threshold, and neither appears in the justification. The blind spot they imply is unstated too: a continuation site indented six to eight would be missed, and none exists today.
items.done_when: The threshold's justification names the two structural numbers that bound it -- the largest legitimate run in the tree and the shallowest continuation indent -- rather than a list of damage magnitudes, and states the blind spot those numbers imply along with the fact that nothing occupies it. A test computes the largest legitimate run across the tree and fails if it has reached the threshold, so the guard reports that its own boundary has stopped being safe instead of silently flagging a table somebody aligned. That test is shown to discriminate by being run against a literal that would breach it. The threshold itself is not moved unless the measurement says it must be, because a number that is correct and badly explained is fixed by explaining it.

items.title: KWB still cannot read a source, and everything needed to build the first extractor is adopted, measured and unused
items.why: KWB-47 declared the extraction contract and its only implementation is Stated, a person typing --says. The README's opening said KWB ingests references until KWB-56 corrected it, and the Trying it section still says there is no extractor, which is the honest statement and the reason this item exists. Everything the first extractor needs is already in XVPE and was measured today at the commit kwb-platform-xvpe already pins, a7eee3c6e, so no rev bump is involved and bumping stays the separate decision the manifest says it is. xvpe-corpus-text carries Chunk, ChunkingStrategy and PageFidelity and depends on xvpe-primitives alone. xvpe-ai-inference carries Conforms, AnswerValue, a recording codec and replay, recording and replay-recording strategies, and depends on xvpe-primitives and xvpe-json-text. Probed in a scratch crate against that pinned SHA: both resolve, both compile, both proved by naming a type from each rather than by the manifest listing them, and cargo tree --no-default-features -e normal shows zero third-party packages in the closure. Neither crate carries a provider, which is what makes the quarantine the owner asked for actually separable, and the replay strategy is what lets this be tested without credentials.
items.done_when: A model-backed reader implements ExtractionStrategy and kwb admit can read a born-digital text source instead of being told what it says. kwb-platform-xvpe stays the one crate permitted to name XVPE and re-exports what is needed, the way it already re-exports the persistent map as VersionedMap; the reader is a band 3 crate that names only kwb-platform-xvpe, and the README bands table gains its row, which tests/contract then asserts in both directions. PageFidelity maps into ReadingKind rather than replacing it, which is what KWB-47 said would happen when a reading adapter arrived. Every test runs on the replay strategy against a committed recording, so the suite needs no credentials and no network, and the recording is evidence rather than a fixture invented to make a test pass. Malformed model output is refused and never becomes a graph mutation, proved against a recording of a real malformed answer rather than a hand-written one. A reader that fails is Unmet and never Barren, proved end to end rather than at the seam. Re-running an extraction over the same source admits the same graph. D-015's third deferral is settled here rather than left: chunking makes a reading cover one passage, so either a reading is per-chunk or ProposedReading carries a location per proposal, and whichever is chosen is stated with what it costs. No provider, no credential and no network dependency enters this workspace.

Declined.reason: Superseded by KWB-66, which the owner re-scoped and reassigned. Two changes. Its territory omitted crates/host/kwb-cli, so the verb that makes a source readable could not have landed under it -- the item as authored could not reach its own done_when. And its completion criterion was quality-shaped where the owner's is functional: KWB reads a real born-digital source automatically, extracts at least one grounded proposition, feeds it through existing identity, admission and storage, and accumulates corroboration across sources without the model bypassing KWB authority. Extraction quality stops being part of the seam. The Fable/DeepSeek split is not abandoned but made operational -- Fable owns the seam because the seam defines meaning, DeepSeek owns the iterations once it exists -- and leaving this parked optimised for an organisational split with no worker on one side while the product could not perform its defining first operation.

items.title: Temporal reconstruction is recorded as met and nothing can reach it, and as written it is not expressible either
items.why: D-012 answers D-008's eight storage requirements and puts requirements 3 and 4 under the heading met, and met structurally, saying temporal reconstruction is the same mechanism as a which-world read -- the version published at an instant is a value that was kept. D-014 then made the graph durable by replaying an append-only record and said that makes D-008's temporal requirement fall out, the graph as of an instant being a prefix of the record. Measured: Replay is called in five places and every one of them passes the whole log. Nothing anywhere takes a prefix, so no user can reach the graph as of anything. The mechanism permits it and the capability does not exist, which is this repository's most-cited defect shape written into a canonical record as a completed requirement. The phrase is wrong too, and more quietly: a publication record carries a kind, a standing, a successor, a reason and the entity, and no time at all. D-014 said kwb-platform is owed a clock for the record's own timestamps and kwb-platform's own module doc says the clock, lock and process ports are not here yet. So as of an instant cannot be asked today in any form, and what a prefix actually answers is as of the first N publications. That is not nothing: merge_losers reports what was merged away and D19-B is the incident where a merge audit could resolve none of it, so seeing the graph before a merge is the capability that incident asks for.

items.title: The measurement D-014 deferred adoption on is made, and it says the blocker is a clock rather than a fit
items.why: D-014 decided the graph becomes durable by replaying an append-only record and deliberately did not adopt xvpe-event-journal, saying: this record does not adopt it, because adopting needs a second measurement nobody has made -- whether a record written for a mining run fits a knowledge publication. Settled by measuring its record shape against a publication, which nothing has done. Nothing has done it since, and it is the one prose-stated condition in this repository that a session can actually discharge: nine others need a reader that splits, a second writer, a corpus where replay time is measurable, or a clock, and none of those exist. Measured against xvpe at the commit kwb-platform-xvpe already pins. EventJournal::Event is generic over WallClockStrategy and writes record.Text(EVENT, kind).Number(AT, Unix_Seconds(clock)), so every record carries a timestamp by construction, and JournalRecord::At documents that a failure to read one means the line was not written by that crate. KWB has no clock. D-014's own consequences say kwb-platform is owed a clock for the record's own timestamps and kwb-platform's module documentation says the clock, lock and process ports are not here yet. So the answer is not that the shapes disagree about knowledge -- it is that KWB cannot write a record of that shape at all. That is the same dependency D-012's amendment named under KWB-60 as what would make a real instant answerable, so two deferrals in two records converge on one port.

items.title: An agent can learn which concept was merged away and cannot learn anything it said
items.why: kwb-mcp answers merge_losers, which reports a closed concept, its successor and the reason that authorised the merge. Measured against a rebuilt binary: after superseding phlogiston into oxidation, merge_losers reports phlogiston pointing at the successor's address with its reason, and neighbours phlogiston reports nothing. The claim it carried is still in the graph -- Versioned keeps it -- and no tool can reach it, because Neighbourhood_Of is on CurrentQueries and a merged concept is not current. HistoricalQueries offers Claims_Matching, Merge_Losers and Concept_Count and no neighbourhood at all. So an audit can establish that something was merged and cannot establish what was lost, which is D19-B one step later than the prototype had it: there merge-audit could not resolve which identifiers had been merged, here they resolve and say nothing. D17 is the rule that destruction requires evidence, and evidence a reader cannot reach is the same shape as the AdmitChunk path disarmed by a default -- an obligation that looks handled because nothing complains. Separately, the tool guard has the asymmetry KWB-61 fixed for verbs: it checks that every tool the README names is declared, not that every declared tool is named, so a tool added without documentation is caught by nothing.
items.done_when: The neighbourhood of a concept is answerable in the historical world, so a merge loser's claims and their citations are reachable, and the query reports the standing of what it returns rather than presenting a closed claim as a live one -- a reader who cannot tell them apart has the confusion D19-B is about. A kwb-mcp tool exposes it, declared in the world it reads like every other, so no caller can ask the historical question of the current graph. Measured end to end against a rebuilt binary on the corpus that produced this finding: phlogiston superseded into oxidation, and the claim it carried reachable with its standing. The tool guard checks both directions, as KWB-61 made the verb guard do, and is shown to discriminate by mutating the real files each way. README names the tool.

items.title: KWB cannot perform its defining first operation: nothing here reads a source and decides what it says
items.why: The README's first line said KWB ingests references until KWB-56 corrected it, and the Trying it section still says there is no extractor. KWB-47 declared the extraction seam and its only implementation is Stated, a person typing --says. Everything else is now measured and cleared: KWB-59 proved xvpe-corpus-text and xvpe-ai-inference resolve and compile at the commit kwb-platform-xvpe pins, by naming a type from each, with zero third-party packages in the closure and no provider in either crate; KWB-64 adopted the clock through the same quarantine; D-015 decided where a reading's provenance may and may not go. InferenceStrategy's own contract says a schema is a constraint and not a suggestion, returning Malformed rather than a non-conforming answer, and ReplayInference::From_Recordings with the recording codec means every test can run offline against committed evidence. So the seam is the remaining work and the seam is where meaning is decided -- what an extractor may propose against what KWB admits, how a reading reaches the single write door, what happens when a model fails. The owner re-scoped this to Fable for that reason: handing over the seam would hand over the part that cannot be re-derived from a prompt, while prompt iteration, schema tuning, fixture generation and corpus sweeps remain volume work for later.

items.title: The binary's own help omits a verb it dispatches and asserts a capability the repository now has, and the guard between surfaces covers two of three
items.why: Measured by running the binary rather than by reading it. kwb help mentions history zero times; the dispatch carries it and README documents it twice. So a person cannot discover the temporal read from the tool itself -- and the README routes them there for exactly that, saying kwb help has the flags, they are not repeated here, because a copy of a help text is a copy that drifts. The copy drifted in the direction the sentence was written to prevent. Second, kwb help still says there is no extractor, nothing here reads the document and decides what it says. KWB-66 built one and KWB-56 corrected that sentence in the README, so the two surfaces now contradict each other and I made that happen by fixing one copy and not the other -- the two-copies defect, committed by the session that has closed it five times. Third, the guard that would have caught either covers README against dispatch, which KWB-61 made bidirectional; it does not read the help text at all, so the surface a person actually runs is checked by nothing.
items.done_when: kwb help names every verb the binary dispatches with the flags each takes, so the README's promise that the help has the flags is true rather than aspirational. Its statement about reading says what is now the case: an extractor exists, this command does not use one, and why -- without implying either that KWB still cannot read or that this command can. A guard reads the help text the binary actually prints rather than the source that prints it, because the defect is that a person running the tool is told something false, and a check on the source would pass on a help string that is assembled and never emitted. Shown to discriminate by mutating the real file for each direction it claims to check, and the collector asserted to have found the verbs, since a guard that reads none passes anywhere.

items.title: The record that decided where a reading's provenance lives says nothing here reads a source, and the extractor shipped an hour later
items.why: D-015 states three deferrals with conditions and a section titled Why it is not built here, which rests on three sentences: nothing in this repository reads a source, every reading is a person through Stated, and today there is exactly one reading per assertion and no two of them can differ. KWB-66 falsified all three. kwb-extract reads sources; ReadsText is a reader that is not a person; a read now returns one reading per passage, and two readers over different models produce different lineage. Measured: D-015 mentions KWB-66 zero times. Its conditions are Settled by the first reader whose readings differ, Settled by the same condition, and Settled by a reader that splits -- and KWB-66 is a reader that splits and whose readings can differ, so all three fired. The third was settled in the extraction contract's own documentation by that item and the record was never told, which is the one-crate-away gap between a decision and the code that answers it. This is KWB-62's shape with a shorter fuse: there a held subject went stale eight minutes after the amendment warning that lists go stale, and here a record's entire reason for not building something was destroyed by the next item but one, both written in this session. The consequence is not cosmetic. A reader of D-015 today is told that readings cannot differ, which is the premise the whole deferral rests on, and would conclude the provenance gap is unreachable rather than live.
items.done_when: D-015 records that all three conditions are met, names KWB-66 in the checkable form so the board guard holds the claim, and replaces the three false sentences rather than leaving them for a reader to disbelieve. What the unstranding costs is stated: a claim admitted from a model now enters the graph with no record of which model or which passage produced it, so the requirement that every admitted claim identifies its source occurrence and extraction protocol is live rather than theoretical -- and the reason it is still not built here is the honest one, that nothing yet produces claims from a model because no provider exists, not the one the record currently gives. The decision itself is untouched: a reading is still its own fact and an assertion still identifies by neither location nor lineage, because the corroboration-count argument that settled that does not depend on any of this.

items.title: The publication log is a bespoke append-only mechanism beside an XVPE one that now exists on the remote
items.why: D-014 decided the graph becomes durable by replaying an append-only record and deliberately did not adopt xvpe-event-journal, naming its condition: measuring the record shape against a publication. KWB-63 made that measurement and found the blocker is a clock rather than a fit; KWB-64 adopted the clock, so the bundle D-014 asked for is down to adoption and migration. Under D-135 an append-only journal is domain-neutral and XVPE owns one, so KWB's FileRecordLog and its separator-delimited positional record are a bespoke restatement -- legitimate only while D-014's deferral stood. The journal rewrite was committed locally at 8ff98a8fd and unpushed, which KWB-67's iteration measured directly as revspec not found, since KWB adopts from the remote. origin/dev has now moved to 8ff98a8fd and a scratch probe resolves and compiles all five adopted crates plus the journal at it. The bump is not free and that is why the manifest calls it a decision rather than maintenance. HamtMap takes three generic parameters where it took two -- Key, Value and a hasher Policy -- and the crate moved from foundations/collections to foundations/data/collections. KnowledgeGraph is built on that type through VersionedMap, and kwb-domain's own reasoning says determinism is enforced by sorting at the boundary rather than by hasher choice, so the Policy is a question this repository must answer out loud rather than fill in. Third-party closure is unchanged: web-time, hashbrown and smallvec, the three D-012 already measured and accepted.
items.done_when: The pin moves to the commit measured here and the workspace builds and passes on it, with the Policy that HamtMap now requires chosen deliberately and the choice written where the determinism argument lives -- because a hasher supplied to satisfy a compiler is exactly the kind of default D20 is about. The publication log is XVPE's journal rather than a bespoke one, and kwb-platform-std keeps no second append-only implementation. A publication becomes a record of that shape, and the migration is faced rather than discovered: a log written before this item either still replays or is refused with something a reader can act on, and which of those it is, is stated. D-014's remaining deferral closes and says what it cost. No new third-party dependency enters beyond the three already accepted.

Declined.reason: Superseded by KWB-71: correct territory, and a why that does not carry the false bump measurement recorded in the abandon reason above.

abandoned.reason: Correcting a false measurement in this item's own why before continuing. It says the bump is not free, that HamtMap takes three generic parameters where it took two, and that the crate moved from foundations/collections to foundations/data/collections. All three are wrong. HamtMap takes Key, Value and Policy at a7eee3c6e as well, kwb-domain already declares VersionedMap with RandomState as its third argument, and the crate sits at foundations/data/collections at both commits. The compiler error that produced the claim came from my scratch probe passing two parameters; I attributed my own code's error to the dependency, which is the instrument-failure hazard this board has recorded twice. Measured properly by bumping the real pin in kwb-platform-xvpe and building the real workspace: it compiles with no source change, 199 tests pass and clippy is clean. The bump is free. Abandoned and re-claimed rather than declined so the false claim and its correction stay visible together, which is what OD-LEDGER-001 records as this board's best property.

Territory is wrong and cannot be amended. The journal owns its own file IO -- EventJournal::Open and Write -- so a journal-backed log names XVPE and must live in kwb-platform-xvpe, the one crate permitted to. That makes the composition root name a different type, and crates/host/kwb-cli is not in this item's territory, so the done_when requiring kwb-platform-std to keep no second append-only implementation is unreachable under it. Same defect that sank KWB-59. Superseded by KWB-71 with kwb-cli added and the why corrected.

items.title: The tool table and the tool registry are two authorities for one fact, and three of five rows already disagree
items.why: The guards this session built check that two artifacts name the same things. They do not check that the two artifacts say the same thing about them, and the gap is already open: TOOLS carries a summary per tool and README carries a column of prose beside each name, and three of the five disagree. neighbours is a concept with its claims and their assertions in the code and their citations in the README; merge_losers is concepts closed against a successor -- the question an audit needs, against concepts closed against a successor, with the reason; held_neighbours drops what a merge loser said. Each is a paraphrase somebody wrote once, and nothing can tell which is current. That is the defect family this session found seven times, stated exactly: two artifacts claim to describe one fact and nothing mechanically proves they still agree. The owner's direction is to stop maintaining two authorities where the fact is an enumeration, and make the document a projection of canonical machine-readable state -- which is also this product's own thesis, since KWB exists to make documentation a projection of structured knowledge rather than a second manually synchronised reality. XVPE has the precedent: its comparison tables are generated by a tool and never hand-edited. Rationale prose still belongs to a person; an enumeration of capabilities does not.
items.done_when: The README's tool table is a projection of TOOLS rather than a copy of it. A check generates the table from the registry and compares it to the README, printing the correct block when they differ so that fixing it is pasting rather than hand-reconciling, and the table is marked as generated so a reader knows not to edit it. Every column is projected, not only the names, because the names already agreed while the prose did not. Shown to discriminate by mutating each side of the real files: a summary changed in the registry, and a row edited in the README. This establishes the pattern rather than completing it; the dispatch to help, the bands table and decision status are the same shape and are named as owed, with the distinction that rationale is not generated and only enumerations are.

items.why: D-014 decided the graph becomes durable by replaying an append-only record and deliberately did not adopt xvpe-event-journal, naming the condition: measure its record shape against a publication. KWB-63 made that measurement and found the blocker was a clock rather than a fit. KWB-64 adopted the clock. The publication log is XVPE's journal: a journal-backed RecordLogStrategy lives in kwb-platform-xvpe because the journal owns its file IO and must be named by the one crate permitted to name XVPE, kwb-platform-std keeps no second append-only implementation, and the composition root names the new one. The port is unchanged -- D-012's own words, a new implementation behind an existing seam and not a change to the seam. A publication becomes a record of the journal's shape, and the migration is faced rather than discovered: a log written before this item still replays, because D-014 made the graph durable BY replay and a format change that orphans existing logs loses the thing it was built for, so the reader accepts both shapes and writes only the new one, and a test replays a pre-existing log copied rather than constructed. abandoned.reason: The adoption is refused on a measurement, and the done_when requiring it cannot be met honestly. EventJournal::Write returns unit and swallows failures -- it prints to standard error and continues, and the crate documents that as deliberate: a write failure is reported to standard error rather than propagated. That is right for what it is. A mining run should not die because its observability journal failed. KWB's publication log is not that. D-014 made the graph durable by replay and says the graph is not reproducible at all, so a lost publication loses information no re-run recovers; KWB-34 built Record_Into to return a Result and kwb admit to fail on it, because a report must not outrun the work. Adopting that write path would mark a run Succeeded when its publications never landed, which is D19 exactly -- the incident this repository's admission pipeline is shaped around. The two are the same shape with opposite failure contracts: an observability record versus a system of record. Detecting the failure through Line_Count before and after would work and would depend on an implementation detail rather than a contract, which is the kind of guarantee this repository refuses to build on. What XVPE would need is a fallible write, and naming that is the D-135-consistent move rather than working around it here. items.title: The verbs are written twice and a guard keeps the copies in step, where one table would leave nothing to keep in step
items.why: Measured in main.rs: each verb appears in the dispatch match and again as a usage line in Print_Usage. Four verbs, two places, and KWB-67 built a guard that runs the binary and compares them in both directions -- which it had to, because the copies had already drifted: history was dispatched and the help named it nowhere, and the help asserted there is no extractor after KWB-66 built one. KWB-70 then showed the stronger move on the MCP tool table, and the owner's direction is to take it generally: where two artifacts describe one enumeration, stop maintaining two authorities and make one a projection of the other. A bidirectional check makes drift detectable and still leaves two places to edit, which is the arrangement that produced the drift. A verb table the dispatch runs from and the help renders from leaves nothing to keep in step, because there is one value. That is also this product's own thesis applied to its own composition root.
items.done_when: One table declares each verb with the usage line a reader is shown, the dispatch runs from it, and Print_Usage renders from it, so the two cannot disagree. Nothing about what a command does moves into the table -- the handlers stay handlers and the prose explaining D17 or coverage stays prose, because only the enumeration is projected. help and its aliases stay outside the table for the reason they are already exempt from the guard: they are how a reader finds the rest rather than a capability to be listed. KWB-67's guard is kept rather than deleted and its reason updated to say what it now covers: with one authority the name direction is structural, and what remains checkable is that the help actually renders the table, since a projection nobody emits is not a projection. Measured against the rebuilt binary, and shown to discriminate by adding a verb to the table and confirming it reaches both the dispatch and the printed help without a second edit.

Declined.reason: Superseded by KWB-74, which is the same work with tests/contract in territory.

abandoned.reason: Territory is one path short and cannot be amended. tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs parses the dispatch by splitting on the match arm's literal, so moving the verbs into a table breaks it, and the workspace cannot be green while it is broken -- which finish requires. The lesson is narrower than the one already recorded. Author items after measuring covered the claim; this is the blast radius. I measured the duplication I was removing and not what else reads the shape I was changing, which a single grep would have shown: three files reference it, and only two are in territory. Measured now: crates/host/kwb-cli/src/main.rs declares it, crates/host/kwb-cli/tests/help.rs reads it, tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs parses it. Superseded by KWB-74 with tests/contract added. The work itself is sound and measured -- one table, the dispatch runs from it, the help renders from it, and adding a fifth verb to the table alone reached both the printed usage and the dispatch with no second edit.

items.why: Measured in main.rs: each verb appeared in the dispatch match and again as a usage line in Print_Usage. Both had to exist because the copies had already drifted: history was dispatched while the help named it nowhere, and the help went on asserting there is no extractor after KWB-66 built one. All three are in territory.

items.title: The bands table is the only place a crate's band exists, and the description guard proves agreement rather than truth
items.why: Two findings, measured. First, the bands table is a second authority with no canonical counterpart: a crate's name comes from the workspace and its Owns column equals its manifest description, both checked in both directions, but the band itself -- 0, 1, 1p, 2, 3, 10 -- is written nowhere except the README. So the one column that cannot be projected is the one that decides the table's shape, and KWB-70 and KWB-74 could not be repeated here without first deciding where a band lives. Second, and sharper: kwb-platform-xvpe's description says it adopts the persistent map versioned state is built on, and it now adopts four XVPE crates -- the persistent map, the clock, the chunker and the inference surface, added by KWB-64, KWB-66 and KWB-72. The README says the same thing and the guard passes, because Test_Every_Crate_Should_Describe_Itself_The_Same_Way_In_Both_Places proves the two copies agree and cannot prove either is true. Two agreeing copies of a stale sentence is what an agreement check is blind to by construction, and it is the argument for projections and the limit of them in one example. Blast radius measured rather than assumed, which is what sank KWB-73: only tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs and README.md read the table or the descriptions, and thirteen manifests carry a description.
items.done_when: A crate's band lives in its own manifest, under package metadata, because a band is a property of the crate and the manifest already holds its description -- so the two halves of a row come from one place. The README's bands table is a projection of the workspace, generated and compared like the tool table, with a marker saying it is generated. Ordering is derived rather than stored: a band sorts by its leading number then its suffix then the crate name, which puts 1 before 1p and 3 before 10 without a second field to keep in step. kwb-platform-xvpe's description says what it now adopts. The description guard is kept and its reason updated to say what it can and cannot show -- that it proves two copies agree, that this is why one stale sentence sat in both, and that a projection removes the agreement question while leaving the truth question to a person. Shown to discriminate by mutating each side of the real files.

items.title: Five records and a module doc state obligations that are discharged or were decided against, so a reader scanning for outstanding work finds phantom debts
items.why: KWB-75 established the limit of every guard here: a projection removes the agreement question and leaves the truth question untouched, and two agreeing copies of a stale sentence pass every check. Applying that as a truth pass over what the records say is still owed, rather than over whether their copies match. Five are discharged and say otherwise. D-008 says a second storage decision is owed and is blocked on the domain types; D-012 made that decision and KWB-3 and KWB-4 closed. D-009 says D-004's held list is owed a correction and that whoever closes KWB-3 should know a boundary design waits on it; the correction is D-004's Two Lists Were Not Enough amendment and KWB-3 is closed. D-010 says the same held list is owed a correction distinguishing its entry as pending from D-009's as stranded, which that amendment made. D-012 says liveness must be one expression and it is owed; Standing::Is_Current is that expression, one definition, guarded by a test that fails on a second. D-014's KWB-63 amendment says KWB has no clock, which KWB-64 falsified an hour later. And kwb-platform's module documentation says the clock, lock and process ports are not here yet and will arrive when something needs them -- the clock never will, because KWB-64 decided to adopt XVPE's through kwb-platform-xvpe rather than declare a rival, which is what D-135 requires. That last one is the dangerous one: a reader following it would build the port the decision exists to prevent. This is the mirror of the stale-premise defect the session has chased. Not a false claim about what the repository can do, but a false claim about what it still has to do, which is worse for a reader deciding what to work on.
items.done_when: Each of the five records says the obligation is discharged and by what, in the checkable Condition met form where an item discharged it, so the board guard holds the claim rather than a reader having to trust it. The sentences are corrected in place rather than deleted, because a record that quietly stops saying something owed leaves no trace that it was. kwb-platform's documentation says the clock is adopted rather than pending, and why -- that a clock has no knowledge-domain semantics so D-135 puts it in XVPE, and that declaring one here would be the rival authority KWB-49, KWB-55 and KWB-61 each removed. It says nothing about the lock and process ports beyond what is true, since neither has been decided either way. Nothing about any decision changes; only the statements of what remains.

items.title: A record's frontmatter carries two fields meant to convey its standing, and one never varies while the other disagrees with the body
items.why: The projection programme's last target was decision status, and measuring it first says the target is not a missing document. It is that the fields meant to carry status do not. All fifteen records read status: accepted -- one value across the whole set, so the field distinguishes nothing, and neither AGENTS.md nor README says what another value would mean or when it would be set. Meanwhile version is hand-maintained and disagrees with the body: D-009 carries one amendment at version 1, D-014 carries two at version 1, and D-012 carries three at version 2, while D-004, D-008 and D-013 each carry one at version 2. So the convention version equals one plus amendments is observed in three records and broken in three, and all three breaks are amendments written in this session -- mine. Nothing reads either field and nothing checks them, which is why the drift was invisible. That is the same family as everything else found here, one level up: a field that looks like a signal and carries none is worse than an absent field, because a reader takes it for maintained. Projecting a status document from this would have projected the wrong thing accurately.
items.done_when: D-009, D-012 and D-014 carry the version their bodies imply, and the convention -- a record's version is one plus the number of amendments it carries, because an amendment is what a new version of a record is here -- is written down where a record author will see it rather than inferred from three examples out of six. A guard fails when a record's version disagrees with its amendment count, shown to discriminate by mutating a real record each way, with a floor asserting it found the records and at least one amendment so it cannot pass by reading nothing. What status means is settled rather than left: either it is given the values that would make it informative and what each means, or it is recorded that it has one value because no record has yet been superseded wholesale and that this is the condition under which it would change. Whichever, a reader can tell what the field is for. Nothing about any decision changes.

Declined.reason: Superseded by KWB-78, which is the same subject with AGENTS.md reserved. Kept visible rather than deleted because the defect that ended it is the one worth reading: an item whose done_when names an artifact its territory does not reserve cannot be finished honestly, and the failure is invisible until the last step.

abandoned.reason: Authored one path short of its own done_when. The clause 'the convention is written down where a record author will see it' has exactly one honest home in this repository -- AGENTS.md, beside the docs/records/ routing row an author reads before writing a record -- and AGENTS.md is not in this item's territory, which is tests/contract plus the three records amended. The three record versions are corrected and the guard is written and mutation-proven in the working tree; what is missing is the sentence that cannot be written from here. Re-authored as KWB-78 with AGENTS.md reserved. Abandoned rather than declined because the work is real and nearly whole, and abandoned rather than quietly widened because KWB-73 was declined for being one path short and writing outside territory would be the same defect with the check removed.

items.title: Four functions in tests/contract share two names and one pair does not share its behaviour, while the library that exists to hold them says so is owed
items.why: KWB-75 created tests/contract/src/lib.rs to stop Repository_Root being written a fifth time, and its own module doc names the rest as owed and not done: boundaries.rs, literals.rs and commands.rs still carry their own copies. Measured now, that debt is real -- four Repository_Root bodies, and boundaries.rs additionally carries a Workspace_Member_Crate_Names identical to the library's Workspace_Members. But the measurement found something the debt note did not say. There are two Quoted_After functions and they are NOT the same function. The library's splits on the prefix anywhere in the text; boundaries.rs's requires a line to BEGIN with it. On today's manifests they agree, which is why nothing noticed, but a prefix appearing in a comment or mid-line parts them -- and boundaries.rs and projections.rs each read manifests believing they are calling the same reader. That is the session's own dominant defect wearing a name instead of a document: two things claim to be one fact and nothing proves they agree. A note saying work is owed is also the phantom-debt shape KWB-76 found, except this one is true, and it stops being true only when the work is done or the note is corrected.
items.done_when: tests/contract has one Repository_Root, one Workspace_Members and one Quoted_After, all in the library, and boundaries.rs, literals.rs and commands.rs use them. The two Quoted_After semantics are reconciled deliberately rather than by whichever body survived the move: which one is kept is stated with the reason, and the discarded one's behaviour is named so a later reader knows the choice was made and not defaulted into. A guard fails when a test file under tests/contract defines its own copy of a reader the library already owns, proven by adding one to a real file and watching it fail, so the duplication cannot regrow silently. The module doc's owed paragraph is replaced by what is actually true once it is done, rather than left describing debt that has been paid.

items.why: AGENTS.md's routing table promises README.md answers what exists, what owns what, which band may depend on which. A field that looks like a signal and carries none is KWB-78's finding one tier down, in the architecture rather than in a record's frontmatter. The rule is measurable rather than inventable, because the workspace already obeys one. Every dependency edge in crates/ lands on a crate in the same band or lower, with no upward edge and no cycle; two edges are same-band and both are legitimate -- kwb-platform-std on kwb-platform, which is an adapter on its port, and kwb-extract on kwb-ingest, which is a reader on the seam it implements. items.title: The version rule KWB-78 wrote down is a record's rule, observations obey a different one, and nothing says either to an observation author
items.why: KWB-78 established that a record's version is one plus its amendment count, wrote it in AGENTS.md, and guarded it. It reads docs/records only. AGENTS.md routes readers to docs/observations as one of three authorities, and that directory is entirely unguarded -- no version check, no status check, nothing. Measured: OD-LEDGER-001 is version 2 and carries ZERO amendment sections, so under the record rule it is broken. It is not broken. Its bump to version 2 was KWB-43, commit 5a28ff5, whose subject is my own observation overstated its finding, and now says what was measured -- a correction made IN PLACE, with no amendment appended. That is coherent with what an observation is. A record keeps a superseded claim visible beside its correction because somebody may have acted on the claim; an observation is a finding that is open until something acts on it, and one that overstated itself should simply say what was measured. So the two kinds genuinely differ, and a reader who learned the rule where KWB-78 put it and applied it to an observation would be wrong. Second measured difference, in the other direction: status carries no signal in a record -- all fifteen read accepted, which KWB-78 recorded -- and in an observation it DOES, because both observations read open and the whole point of an observation is that it closes when something acts on it. The field that is inert in one directory is load-bearing in the other, and nothing anywhere says that either. This is KWB-78's own finding one directory across: fields that look like signals, in a routed authority nothing checks.
items.done_when: AGENTS.md says what version and status mean for an OBSERVATION, beside where it already says what they mean for a record, and says it without implying the record rule applies: an observation's version counts revisions made in place, because an observation is a finding that is corrected rather than a decision whose superseded claims must stay visible, and its status is open until something acts on the finding. The record paragraph is made explicitly about records so a reader cannot carry it across. A guard covers docs/observations: every observation declares a status and a version, and the status is one the convention names. It is shown to discriminate by mutating a real observation each way, and carries a floor asserting it found the observations so it cannot pass by reading nothing. It is demonstrated that the KWB-78 record guard does NOT fire on observations and that this is deliberate rather than an accident of which directory it happens to read. The relation question OD-LEDGER-002 raised is NOT answered here -- that is a separate obligation and mixing it in is the defect KWB-80 recorded. Nothing about any decision or any observation's findings changes.

KWB-86 widened the relation guards to read docs/observations, so the note's phrase no record is now narrower than what actually fails: an entry may be an observation, and an observation may declare a relation. Correcting one copy would make it the one that disagrees with ten, which is why KWB-86 left it. items.title: The root manifest explains its one host dependency in a sentence that lost both crates it names, and the scanner for a sentence that lost content has a floor four times the damage
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-13. Cargo.toml line 66 reads `# The hosts.  is here because  projects its tool registry into the` - two two-space gaps where two backtick-delimited crate names were. `git log -L66,66:Cargo.toml` shows the line was born that way in cdd0caa (KWB-70) and no later edit touched it, so the authoring write is what ate them; backticks survived on twelve other added lines in that same commit, so the cause is that one file write and not the commit.

What the sentence said is recoverable and true. `tests/contract` is the only crate in the workspace that depends on `kwb-mcp` - one edge, tests/contract/Cargo.toml line 17 - and tests/contract/tests/projections.rs uses `kwb_mcp::TOOLS` to project the README tool table, which is why a composition root is in `[workspace.dependencies]` at all.

Nothing here can see the damage. tests/contract/tests/literals.rs is this workspace's one instrument for a sentence that lost content, and its `GAP` is 8 - a floor its own doc comment justifies structurally as sitting above every legitimate run, measured at 5. This damage carries 2. Sweeping every tracked .rs, .toml, .md, .json and .yml file for mid-line runs of two to seven spaces returns this line and about forty legitimate ones: column layout in the README sample output, println! alignment in kwb-cli, and deliberate double-space fixtures in kwb-domain. A threshold low enough to catch this fires on all of them, so run length is the wrong instrument for damage this shallow and lowering the number is not the fix. No guard is proposed, on the same ground the Band 0 note in kwb-contracts/src/lib.rs was left alone: one instance, and no measured rule to hold it to.

One reading was checked and dropped rather than carried into this item: the -- in the same comment is not damage. It appears 234 times in work/ledger.json and in nearly every file in the tree, beside em dashes throughout.
items.done_when: Cargo.toml no longer carries a sentence that names neither crate it is about. The two lost names are restored, and the reasoning that sentence went on to duplicate is not: tests/contract/Cargo.toml already states why that edge exists, beside the edge, and AGENTS.md step 5 forbids introducing a second authority for something already governed. So the root manifest keeps only what is its own - that a composition root depended on by a check is an unusual workspace shape - and points at the manifest holding the rest. `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` passes, which shows the manifest still parses and every boundary guard still reads it. That is not evidence the sentence is true; both names in it were verified against the workspace separately, as recorded above.

items.title: The workspace declares a minimum Rust version it does not compile on, and the two releases between the claim and the truth are imported through the crate that exists to quarantine XVPE
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-13 on Linux, against four toolchains, with a target directory of its own so nothing contended: `cargo +1.85.0 check --workspace --all-targets` fails, 1.86.0 fails, 1.87.0 passes, 1.88.0 passes. Cargo.toml line 51 says `rust-version = "1.85"`. The true floor is 1.87.0, so the declared value is wrong by two releases.

Whose floor it is, measured rather than assumed. `cargo +1.85.0 check -p kwb-contracts -p kwb-model -p kwb-platform --lib` exits 0: this repository's own lowest crates do compile on the declared version. What fails is `xvpe-collections-map`, on six uses of the unstable library feature `integer_sign_cast`, stabilized in 1.87. `cargo tree -i` puts it at xvpe-collections-map <- xvpe-collections-persistent <- kwb-platform-xvpe, and from there into kwb-domain, kwb-retrieval, kwb-ingest, kwb-extract, kwb-mcp, kwb-cli and kwb-contract-tests - every crate above band 1p.

That is the fact worth keeping. `D-007` adopts XVPE by git reference into a crate that exists to quarantine it, and structurally the quarantine holds: the XVPE edge is declared in exactly one manifest and `Test_Only_The_Quarantine_Crate_Should_Name_Xvpe` proves it. The toolchain floor that edge carries is not quarantined. It propagates to every dependent, it is set by a pinned commit in another repository, and it moves silently when the pin moves.

What the wrong number costs is a refusal that fires for the wrong reason. `rust-version` is what Cargo reads to refuse a too-old toolchain by name. Declaring 1.85 means a contributor on 1.85 or 1.86 is not told the toolchain is too old; they get E0658 six times from inside a dependency they did not add and cannot see from this workspace.

Not in this item, and named so it is not mistaken for done: this repository pins no toolchain at all. XVPE pins nightly and Nomos pins 1.88.0 exactly, each with its reason written beside it, and Nomos cites OD-GATE-012 for pinning the toolchain the same way it pins everything it depends on. Whether this repository follows is a decision and belongs in a record, not in a correction that only makes an existing number true.
items.done_when: Cargo.toml declares the minimum Rust version this workspace actually compiles on, which was measured as 1.87.0 and is not 1.85. Nothing else changes: no toolchain file is added, because that is a decision this item does not make. `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` passes, which shows the manifest still parses and every boundary guard still reads it. That predicate is not evidence of the floor and is not offered as any - the floor was established by building the workspace on 1.85.0, 1.86.0, 1.87.0 and 1.88.0 directly, as recorded above.

items.title: Six pushes have run the gate and no step has ever executed, and independently of that the gate as configured cannot resolve the dependency D-007 adopts
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-13. Two independent facts, either of which alone stops the gate.

First: no step has ever run. Six workflow runs exist on dev, 34736068864 through 34766510019, every one `completed failure` in four or five seconds with an empty steps array. GitHub's annotation on each is the same: the job was not started because recent account payments have failed or the spending limit needs increasing. That is an account condition and nothing in this repository can change it.

Second, and the part that outlives the billing: the gate as written could not pass anyway. `kwb-platform-xvpe` adopts four crates from github.com/kevinmettias/xvpe, which is private. .github/workflows/gate.yml provides no credential for it - no `token:` on checkout, no ssh-agent, no `net.git-fetch-with-cli` - and this workspace has no .cargo/config.toml. The token `actions/checkout@v4` installs is scoped to this repository, and cargo does not use it for a git dependency. Reproduced on Linux: `cargo fetch` fails with `failed to authenticate when downloading repository`. The pin is not at fault, and that was checked rather than assumed - 8ff98a8fd is present on xvpe's origin/dev.

What the gate would have reported was measured by hand instead, on Linux, with xvpe's git database seeded from a machine that has credentials and with a target directory of its own: all three steps pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on stable 1.98.0, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` is 210 passed and 0 failed, and `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` exits 0. The test count is identical to Windows and the name sets are identical too, so nothing here is platform-conditional; the workspace declares no cfg gate anywhere.

One number in that paragraph was wrong before it was right, and it is recorded because the failure is instructive. The first Linux run reported 230. Two cargo processes were running against one CARGO_TARGET_DIR and writing one log path, and their interleaved output summed to more tests than exist. Re-measured in isolation it is 210. A measurement taken while something else is building is not a measurement.

Why this is worth writing down rather than leaving in a session. `D-005` adopted the nomos ledger partly on the strength of the gate: `nomos work finish` refuses at exit 4 when gate.yml cannot be read, on the grounds that an item finished against a check weaker than the gate is the defect that refusal exists to prevent. That refusal is satisfied by the file being readable. Seventy-seven items have been finished against it and it has never proved anything, because the check it stands for has not run once.

This observation makes no decision. Restoring the gate needs an account change and a credential decision about granting CI read access to a private repository, and both are the maintainer's rather than a session's.
items.done_when: docs/observations/ carries an observation stating the two measured facts, the reproduction, and the hand measurement that stands in for the gate, with `status: open` because nothing has acted on it. It declares a relation to `D-005`, whose stated precondition it is about, and `D-005` carries the other end in its Referenced By list, since a relation reachable from one side only is the defect `KWB-38` measured. No decision is recorded and no remedy is applied: the credential question is not a session's to answer. `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` passes, which is the real predicate here - it is the suite that checks an observation declares a version and a meaningful status, that a declared relation is reachable from both ends, and that a Referenced By section carries the derived note.

items.title: This repository pins the commit of every dependency it adopts and pins no toolchain, and the floor it compiles on is set by a crate in another repository
items.why:
Authored from the measurement in `KWB-90` rather than ahead of it. That item established, by building the workspace on four toolchains, that the floor is 1.87.0 and that it is imported: this repository's own lowest crates compile on 1.85, and what raises the floor is `xvpe-collections-map`, reached through `kwb-platform-xvpe`, using `integer_sign_cast`. `KWB-90` corrected the declared number and deliberately stopped there, because what follows is a decision and not a correction.

The decision. This repository has no rust-toolchain.toml. Both siblings have one and both wrote their reason beside it: XVPE pins `channel = "nightly"` because its brace style needs an unstable rustfmt option, and Nomos pins `channel = "1.88.0"` exactly, citing OD-GATE-012, on the stated grounds that it pins a toolchain the same way it pins everything else it depends on. That argument transfers here without modification: `D-007` adopts XVPE by commit SHA precisely so reproducibility does not depend on another working tree, and leaving the toolchain to whatever rustup happens to default to on a given machine leaves the other half of the same question open.

What is already known, so this does not re-measure it. The floor is 1.87.0. Windows and Linux agree on 210 tests and on the test name sets. Linux resolved to stable 1.98.0 and was clean under `-D warnings`. So the spread between the floor and a current stable is eight releases wide and nothing currently fails anywhere in it.

What genuinely needs deciding, and why it is not obvious. Pinning to the measured floor makes every build the floor build and stops anyone noticing when newer toolchains break. Pinning to a current stable abandons the floor claim `rust-version` makes. Pinning nothing is today's state and means the gate, if it ever runs, tests whatever ubuntu-latest shipped that morning. `OD-GATE-001` is relevant and does not settle it: the gate has never executed, so no pin has ever been exercised by CI, and a toolchain decision made to serve CI would be serving something that does not currently run.

A caution this repository has already paid for once. `D-004` holds that a decision depending on an open inventory does not proceed. The inventory here is closed - the floor is measured, both sibling precedents are read, and the consequence of each option is stated above - so this is claimable. What is not settled is which option the maintainer wants, and a session that picks one should record the alternatives it refused, with reasons, the way every other record here does.
items.done_when: A record in docs/records/ decides whether this repository pins a toolchain and, if it does, to what and why, naming the alternatives refused and the conditions that would reopen it - the shape every record here already has. If the decision is to pin, rust-toolchain.toml exists and carries its reason beside it as both siblings' do, and the pinned version is one the workspace was built on rather than one inferred from `rust-version`. If the decision is not to pin, that is recorded too, because the absence of a toolchain file currently reads as an omission rather than a choice and that is the ambiguity this item exists to end. The record declares its relations and the other ends carry it back, and `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` passes, which is the suite that checks exactly that.

Declined.reason: Territory is wrong in the way KWB-77 is on this board for: the done_when names rust-toolchain.toml and the territory reserves only docs/records, so the item as written cannot be completed inside what it reserves. It also predates the measurement that decides the components field - cargo fmt --check reports 864 sites where stable rustfmt would collapse this workspace's Allman braces - which belongs in the item rather than arriving after it. Re-authored as KWB-93 reserving docs/records and rust-toolchain.toml, and amending D-007 for the back-link the relation guard requires.

Why a pin at all. D-007 adopts XVPE by commit SHA so that reproducibility does not depend on another repository's working tree. The toolchain is the other half of that same question and is currently left to whatever rustup defaults to on a given machine. Nomos pins channel = 1.88.0 exactly and says it pins a toolchain the same way it pins everything else it depends on, citing OD-GATE-012; XVPE pins nightly because its brace style needs an unstable rustfmt option. This repository mirrors Nomos's conventions deliberately - its lint policy block says so - and is the only one of the three that pins nothing.

What the components field must not contain, measured rather than assumed. cargo +1.87.0 fmt --all --check exits 1 with 864 diff sites, and the diffs are this workspace's Allman braces being collapsed to K and R. There is no rustfmt.toml here to prevent it and stable rustfmt cannot express the style at all - XVPE needs nightly's brace_style = AlwaysNextLine for exactly this. Declaring rustfmt in the pin would install, for every contributor, the one tool that silently reformats the entire workspace away from its own style. The gate needs clippy and nothing here needs rustfmt.

What this item does not settle, named so it is not mistaken for settled: that cargo fmt is destructive here is not fixed by leaving rustfmt out of the components list, because a contributor with a global rustfmt still has it. Both siblings say so in prose and this repository says it nowhere. That is its own item.
items.done_when: A record in docs/records/ decides whether this repository pins a toolchain, to what, and why, naming the alternatives refused and the conditions that would reopen it, in the shape every record here has. rust-toolchain.toml exists, pins a version the workspace was actually built and linted on rather than one inferred from rust-version, and carries its reason beside it as both siblings' do. The record declares its relation and D-007 carries the other end, because a relation reachable from one side only is the defect KWB-38 measured. The record has no Referenced By section, because nothing points at it yet and Test_A_Record_Has_A_Referenced_By_Section_Exactly_When_Something_Points_At_It requires the section exactly when something does. cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests passes, which is the suite that checks the relation, the status, the version against amendments, and the note.

items.title: A command every Rust contributor types would reformat 864 sites away from this workspace's brace style, and nothing here stops it or says so
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-13 on Linux against the pinned 1.87.0. `cargo fmt --all --check` exits 1 with 864 diff sites, and every diff is the same edit: this workspace's Allman braces collapsed onto the declaration line. `cargo fmt` is not an exotic command - it is the one a contributor types by reflex, and here it silently rewrites the entire workspace away from its own style.

Nothing in this repository prevents it and nothing warns about it. There is no rustfmt.toml, and README.md, AGENTS.md and docs/ mention rustfmt, cargo fmt, Allman and brace styling exactly zero times - grepped, not assumed. Both siblings handle this and this repository is the one that does not: XVPE carries a rustfmt.toml pinning nightly's `brace_style = "AlwaysNextLine"`, and Nomos carries one plus a stated prohibition in its README conventions.

`D-016` addressed half of it an hour ago by leaving rustfmt out of the pinned components, and said in as many words that this half remained: a contributor whose global toolchain already carries rustfmt still has the loaded tool. That is the gap this item closes, and it is closed mechanically rather than by prose.

The mechanism was measured before being proposed, which matters because the obvious fix does not exist: stable rustfmt cannot express Allman at all, so no formatting configuration can make `cargo fmt` correct here. What it can do is make it do nothing. `disable_all_formatting` is a stable rustfmt option, and `cargo fmt --all --check -- --config disable_all_formatting=true` exits 0 with 0 diff sites across this workspace, against 864 without it. So the destructive command becomes a no-op rather than a prohibition somebody has to remember.

Why no test guards this, stated rather than left as an omission. The only honest guard would run `cargo fmt --all --check` itself, and that requires rustfmt to be installed - which `D-016` deliberately stopped shipping. A predicate that fails on a machine without rustfmt would be failing for the wrong reason, which this board already holds to be worse than passing for the wrong one. The rustfmt.toml is the mechanism; it is not a claim that needs one.
items.done_when: rustfmt.toml exists at the workspace root, disables formatting outright, and carries its reason beside it - specifically that it is not a formatting configuration and this workspace is not rustfmt-formatted, so that a reader does not mistake it for one. After it, `cargo fmt --all --check` exits 0 where it previously exited 1 with 864 diff sites, and that is run and recorded rather than assumed. `cargo test -p kwb-contract-tests` passes, which shows nothing about formatting and is not offered as if it did - it shows the workspace still parses and every boundary guard still reads it. The formatting proof is the fmt run itself, named here so it can be repeated.

items.title: Two subjects D-004 calls stranded have had their stated unstranding conditions shipped, and the guard built for exactly this rot deliberately cannot see them
items.why:
D-004 v2 sorts held subjects into four states and says a stranded entry is not progressing. Three entries are stranded. KWB-62 corrected one -- the canonical Knowledge IR -- and built Test_Every_Condition_A_Record_Calls_Met_Should_Be_Met_On_The_Board so the list would stop rotting. That guard reads only a line beginning `**Condition met:**`, and its own doc comment says why: the other condition-like passages are not conditions, and a guard that is wrong half the time is switched off. That reasoning is right, and it leaves the other two entries uncovered, because their conditions are not board items at all. Both are written `*Unstranded by:*` and both name a change to xvpe.

Both changes have landed. Measured against xvpe `dev` `7ec036c52`, committed and pushed:

Cross-source corroboration. D-004 says it is unstranded by the miner acquiring a second, source-excluding claim identity, and that this is a change to the instrument rather than a longer run of it. `xvpe-corpus-ledger` ships `ClaimAssertion::Of(assertion)`, which folds in the assertion and nothing else; its doc comment argues the case in this record's own terms and names `SourceClaimIdentity` as the contrast it is built against. `ClaimLedger` carries `Support_For`, `Corroborated`, `Novel` and `Restatements` -- the support count and the falling-rate measurement D-004 says are unmeasurable while every claim is unique by construction. `xvpe-brainstorm-synthesizer/src/main.rs:1122` reads `Corroborated()` in the live binary, not a test.

Coverage and exhaustion. D-004 says it is unstranded by a coverage ledger that is read rather than another sweep, and that no `coverage`, `resume` or `redundant` symbol exists in either product. `CorpusLedger` ships `Has_Ever_Seen`, which is the nobody-looked versus looked-and-found-nothing distinction by name, with `Settlement_Of`, `UnitSettlement` and `SettlementCounts` partitioning units into answered, unanswerable and work-remaining. `xvpe-reference-miner/src/main.rs:1060` reads `Settlement_Of` in the live binary, and `xvpe-mining-memory` carries resume with tests over it. Both products depend on both crates.

So the stranded category is empty, and the amendment that predicted this rot by name is the thing that rotted. It measured at `a7eee3c6e`; `kwb-platform-xvpe` pins `8ff98a8fd`; the two crates landed at `7ec036c52`. The instrument moved twice and the pin moved once, and nothing here noticed either.

This is a re-sort, which D-004 authorises in its own words -- revised when the miner's relevant experiments close, by moving entries from the second list to the first -- and it is not a decision about any held subject. Semantic reconciliation is untouched by every measurement above, so this does not reach KWB-82.
items.done_when: D-004 is at version 3 and nothing it calls stranded is stranded. Both entries move to Pending rather than to safe-to-proceed, because the instrument can now answer these questions and has not yet been run at scale to produce the answers, and the amendment states which of those two things it is claiming for each. Every claim names the xvpe SHA it was measured at, since the last amendment's did not survive the pin moving. The amendment also states what the KWB-62 guard does not cover and why, so that the next reader is not told this list is machine-checked when the half of it that just rotted cannot be. It does not move semantic reconciliation, which no measurement here touches, and it does not weaken the rule the record exists for.

items.title: The manifest names four XVPE crates and this workspace compiles nine, and both surprises this repository has had came from the five it does not name
items.why:
`D-007` adopts XVPE by git reference and commit SHA into a crate that exists to quarantine it. The manifest names four: `xvpe-collections-persistent`, `xvpe-clock`, `xvpe-corpus-text`, `xvpe-ai-inference`. `Cargo.lock` resolves nine -- those four plus `xvpe-collections-handle`, `xvpe-collections-map`, `xvpe-collections-sequence`, `xvpe-json-text` and `xvpe-primitives`. The five are named nowhere in this repository.

The manifest states its own rule beside the pin: *Bumping the `rev` is a decision, not maintenance. What changed between two commits of another repository is exactly what a pinned dependency exists to make visible.* The pin moved from `a7eee3c6e361371b269217201233a2e7d7e36122` to `8ff98a8fd` at `KWB-72`, whose subject was D-014's last deferral, and nothing recorded what the move changed. No record mentions `8ff98a8fd` at all; `OD-GATE-001` does, to say the gate cannot fetch it.

Measured between the two commits: the four named crates did not change. `xvpe-json-text` did -- two consts widened to `pub(crate)`, and an additive method on `JsonRecordReader` with tests. That is behaviourally inert for this workspace, and it is luck rather than a finding, because nothing here established it then and nothing has since. It is also worth saying the first probe run for this was wrong: a per-crate `git diff --stat` pathspec reported `xvpe-json-text` unchanged while the full diff showed it changed, and the crate had moved directories. The instrument was wrong before the conclusion was.

This is the second time an unnamed crate has decided something here. `KWB-90` measured the build floor at 1.87 and traced it to `integer_sign_cast` in `xvpe-collections-map`, reached through `xvpe-collections-persistent`; `D-016` records that the quarantine confines the dependency *edge* but not the toolchain floor that edge carries. Different crate, different axis, same shape, and both were found only by going and looking.

The abbreviated `rev` is not the defect and is not treated as one. `Cargo.lock` resolves it to `8ff98a8fd478750ca4f8a96ffd7174db902ffd0f`, so the abbreviation is latent rather than live, and rewriting it would churn the lock for no measured gain.
items.done_when:
`D-007` records the bump as the measurement the manifest says a pin exists to produce: which commit to which, that the four named crates were unchanged, that `xvpe-json-text` changed and how, and that the change was behaviourally inert -- measured rather than assumed, and dated.

It states the rule that measurement forces: the surface a rev bump must be measured against is the closure `Cargo.lock` resolves, not the crates the manifest names, and it names the five so that the next session does not have to re-derive them. It records this as the second instance of the shape `D-016` named once, since one instance was judged not to need a guard and two is a different question.

A contract guard holds the four `rev` values to a single commit, so a partial bump -- the shape a hand edit inside an item about something else produces -- fails instead of adopting two commits at once. Proven by mutating the real manifest rather than a reconstruction, with every assertion shown able to fail.

It does not change the pin, does not touch `Cargo.lock`, and does not bump anything. The item is the record and the guard.
